lines.en: Luisa, you spent a year in Madrid, whose universities attract students from everywhere. Was it worth the cost?
lines.pt: Luisa, você passou um ano em Madri, cujas universidades atraem estudantes do mundo todo. Valeu o custo?

lines.en: Absolutely, Ida. I stayed with a family whose daughter studied law, and she introduced me to her friends.
lines.pt: Com certeza, Ida. Fiquei com uma família cuja filha estudava Direito e ela me apresentou aos amigos dela.

lines.en: That sounds lucky. My cousin, whose Spanish is perfect now, says the first months were lonely.
lines.pt: Que sorte. Meu primo, cujo espanhol está perfeito agora, diz que os primeiros meses foram solitários.

lines.en: They were for me too, but my professor, whose lectures were fascinating, encouraged me to join a language club.
lines.pt: Para mim também, mas meu professor, cujas aulas eram fascinantes, me incentivou a entrar num clube de idiomas.

lines.en: Did you meet many people there, people whose lives were very different from yours?
lines.pt: Você conheceu muita gente lá, pessoas cujas vidas eram muito diferentes da sua?

lines.en: Yes, a Moroccan student whose parents run a bakery, and a Korean girl whose dream was to become a diplomat.
lines.pt: Sim, um estudante marroquino cujos pais têm uma padaria, e uma coreana cujo sonho era se tornar diplomata.

lines.en: Fascinating. And the money? My mother, whose savings are limited, keeps asking how much a year abroad costs.
lines.pt: Fascinante. E o dinheiro? Minha mãe, cujas economias são limitadas, não para de perguntar quanto custa um ano no exterior.

lines.en: Honestly, the cost surprised me, although I received a small scholarship, which helped with the rent.
lines.pt: Sinceramente, o custo me surpreendeu, embora eu tenha recebido uma pequena bolsa, o que ajudou com o aluguel.

lines.en: Which was the hardest part, apart from money? The language, or being far from home?
lines.pt: Qual foi a parte mais difícil, além do dinheiro? O idioma ou ficar longe de casa?

lines.en: Being far from home, which I had not expected. My grandmother, whose birthday I missed, still teases me about it.
lines.pt: Ficar longe de casa, o que eu não esperava. Minha avó, cujo aniversário perdi, ainda me provoca por isso.

lines.en: You must tell her stories at dinner. Come to my place on Saturday, and bring photos!
lines.pt: Você deve contar histórias a ela no jantar. Venha à minha casa no sábado e traga fotos!

facts.sub: A family whose daughter studied law. My cousin, whose Spanish is perfect, lives abroad.

facts.label: whose + substantivo
facts.sub: Whose liga uma pessoa ou coisa ao que lhe pertence: a student whose parents run a bakery. Em português: “cujo/cuja”. Use para singular e plural.

facts.label: , whose …,

items.s: We say “a student which parents run a bakery”.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.

answers: Whose shows possession. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “a student which parents run a bakery”. → Falso (We say a student whose parents run a bakery.)
Non-defining clauses use commas. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

I stayed with a family whose daughter studied law, and she introduced me to her friends.” says Luisa. “That sounds lucky. My cousin, whose Spanish is perfect now, says the first months were lonely.” says Ida.
